correctness.rationale: Reconstructed degree-pair interpolation: any 16-edge graph with one degree >=8 or two degrees on the same side summing >=8 has an 8-edge induced bipartite subgraph; any degree submultiset summing 8 works by taking all opposite vertices. If no such split, integer partitions on either side are necessarily P=(4,3,3,3,3) or Q=(3,3,3,3,3,1). This is an order-independent argument despite unbounded isolated vertices. Independently wrote, compiled and executed a different column-mask exhaustive C++ generator, not the supplied row-mask code, over ALL four residual fixed degree-sequence matrices: 906, 6720, 6720, 43440, total 57,786; every single matrix admits a row+column subset containing exactly eight ones. Smaller dyadic half-splits 2,4,8 follow stars and pair interpolation. Recursive binary query split of a 2^r-edge subfamily constructs a depth-r shattered tree. Any arbitrary m in [1,31] contains 2^floor(log2 m) edges, and adding hypotheses cannot decrease Ldim; info bound 2^r<=m supplies equality. Upper bound valid for all finite hypothesis classes. Finite exhaustive program alone is not a proof for arbitrary orders: the explicit prior degree-partition reduction provides the needed unbounded-vertex link. No claim at 32 or more edges.
residual_risks: Computer-assisted exhaustive finite case proof depends on the correctness of both degree reduction and enumerator; independently implemented column masks agreed with the source counts and witness property.
No extension to 32 edges, and no claim of any 512-edge general solution.

Its consequence is a complete sharp online mistake-dimension law through 31 edge hypotheses. This is a natural classification of the binary query capability, not an unmotivated arbitrary slice; larger dyadic thresholds remain open or unclaimed.
